assumptions: Assay reagents (capture antibodies/beads, particle counter) behave consistently across buffer conditions or appropriate assay-interference controls will identify reagent-buffer interactions.
Sufficient material yield exists to perform parallel analytic comparisons across process conditions.
biological_rationale: Intact-EV membrane integrity and surface-marker display are candidate determinants of a membrane-protected, EV-associated analytical signature that MISEV2023 recommends verifying with orthogonal assays. Process-induced membrane disruption (freeze-thaw, surfactant exposure, buffer ionic-strength/pH shifts) could convert EV-associated signal to soluble, detergent-insensitive marker signal and thereby decouple particle counts from intact-EV identity and potency linkage. Inference: maintaining an intact-EV signature during downstream processing is required for treating a fraction as an EV-enriched drug substance.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks + detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) measured pre/post-process exposures.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Process-sensitive preservation of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature is proposed as a process-sensitive identity attribute to gate downstream manufacturing decisions and potency assay linkage.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: attribute is conceptually supported but requires experimental verification under process conditions.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent loss of capture-positive signal after processing could reflect selective loss of a minor particle subpopulation or assay interference (e.g., buffer components affecting capture reagents) rather than true membrane disruption.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed, controlled comparison of orthogonal intact-EV signature before and after defined process exposures with appropriate buffer-only and reagent-interference controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV2023 recommends orthogonal intact-EV analytics and highlights sensitivity of EV-associated measures to handling; rodent studies note activity but do not link to specific processing sensitivities.

edges.competing_explanation: Even if signature loss is demonstrated, alternative mitigations (e.g., reformulation or immediate capture) might be required instead of defining acceptance windows.
edges.missing_experiment: Pilot manufacturing-scale runs applying the defined gates to confirm yield and assay robustness under near-GMP conditions.
edges.uncertainty: Inference-level: establishing process gates follows if an analytically reproducible signature can be preserved; uncertainty remains about quantitative acceptance limits and transferability across source-cell lots.

nodes.statement: Downstream processing exposures (number of freeze-thaw cycles and contact with candidate formulation buffers) can alter membrane integrity, surface-marker accessibility, and particle:protein characteristics of MSC-conditioned-medium-derived material.

If membrane integrity and surface-marker display are lost, the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) will be abolished while bulk particle counts may remain similar.

Preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature through defined downstream-process conditions enables use of that signature as a process gate for drug-substance definition and supports development of potency-linked assays.

competing_explanations: Loss of capture-positive co-localization could be caused by simple assay interference from buffer components rather than true membrane disruption.
Observed changes could reflect removal of a minor, highly bioactive particle subpopulation during processing rather than wholesale membrane disruption of the dominant particle population.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned-medium lots (same passage/bank)
Access to validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Laboratory capability for density-fractionation and protection assays
design_question: Daily question: Which specific downstream processing step(s) (controlled freeze-thaw cycles and exposure to candidate nasal formulation buffers) cause loss of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) independent of bulk particle counts?
expected_measurable_effect: Defined downstream exposures (e.g., >1 freeze-thaw cycle or contact with specific buffer classes) will qualitatively abolish co-localization of capture-positive signal with particle-count peaks and render captured signal insensitive to detergent + protease/RNase protection assays while bulk particle counts change minimally.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow per MISEV-style guidance: (1) density-fractionation (iodixanol cushion or gradient) and particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) capture-reagent buffer-compatibility assessment.
experiment.comparator: Matched aliquots from the same enriched small-EV preparation: (A) no-process-exposure control, (B) 1 freeze-thaw, (C) 3 freeze-thaw, (D) incubation with formulation-buffer A, (E) formulation-buffer B, (F) formulation-buffer C, and combinations (e.g., 3 freeze-thaw + buffer exposure). Positive control: characterized small EVs handled identically. Negative control: buffer-only.
experiment.control: Buffer-only controls; detergent-disrupted samples as assay-positive disruption controls; capture-reagent compatibility panels (capture + buffer only) to identify assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of �3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank
Access to validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Analytical capacity for density-fractionation and protection assays
Sufficient material yield for matrixed condition testing
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible qualitative difference in orthogonal intact-EV signature across all tested downstream exposures compared with no-exposure controls across independent replicates, or apparent losses are attributable to assay interference by formulation buffers per compatibility controls.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criterion is met, the hypothesis that the tested downstream processing exposures deterministically disrupt the intact-EV analytical signature is falsified; the program should deprioritize these specific process steps as primary drivers of signature loss and investigate alternative causes (e.g., upstream source-cell variability, fractionation method) or focus on assay-buffer compatibility remediation.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Controlled downstream processing exposures (defined freeze-thaw cycles and contact with specific formulation buffer classes) will abolish the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) in MSC-conditioned-medium-derived materials, even when bulk particle counts are similar.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss (or preservation) of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in post-exposure samples compared with unexposed control. Report whether co-localization is preserved, diminished, or abolished while bulk particle counts remain similar.
experiment.question: Which downstream process exposures (freeze-thaw cycles; contact with candidate nasal formulation buffers of varying pH/ionic strength/surfactant content) cause loss of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature while leaving bulk particle counts relatively unchanged?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed to produce an enriched small-EV fraction (SEC/UC) prior to downstream exposures

Aliquots of the enriched small-EV fraction subjected to matrixed process exposures: 0, 1, 3 freeze-thaw cycles; contact (incubation) for defined time with candidate formulation buffers representing a matrix of pH (acidic/neutral/basic), ionic strength (low/physiologic/high), and surfactant content (none/low non-ionic surfactant)
Purified small-EV positive control (commercial characterized small EVs or lab-validated preparation)
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption
Total protein assay reagents and buffers
Buffer-only controls and capture-reagent compatibility control panels
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio per fraction pre/post exposure
Capture-signal-to-noise in buffer compatibility panels to detect assay interference
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n �3 independent conditioned-medium preps)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In �3 independent conditioned-medium preparations, at least one defined process exposure condition (e.g., �3 freeze-thaw cycles or a specific formulation-buffer class) reproducibly abolishes the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and captured signal becomes detergent/protease-insensitive) while bulk particle counts change minimally compared with no-exposure control; assay-interference controls verify that signal loss is not due to direct capture-reagent incompatibility with buffer components.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Orthogonal intact-EV analytics (capture + particle co-localization + detergent/protease protection) are more sensitive to process-induced membrane disruption than bulk particle counting.
Inference: Process-stage conditions that abolish the intact-EV signature will invalidate downstream potency-linkage assumptions unless mitigated.
falsification_criteria: Failure to observe any qualitative difference in the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature between pre- and post-processing conditions across independent replicates (n �3) and across multiple buffer classes despite applying stressors (freeze-thaw, ionic/pH shifts)—i.e., capture-positive co-localization and detergent/protease sensitivity persist irrespective of tested downstream exposures—would falsify the hypothesis that these process steps are determinative for signature loss.

If assay-interference controls indicate that apparent signature loss is due to reagent-buffer interactions rather than particle membrane disruption, the hypothesis as stated is falsified and must be reframed to focus on assay compatibility rather than process sensitivity.
human_decisions_required: Select 2–3 candidate nasal formulation buffer prototypes to include in the exposure matrix.
Define acceptable qualitative pass/fail criteria for retention of the orthogonal intact-EV signature for process acceptance.
Decide whether to prioritize freeze-thaw avoidance or buffer reformulation based on experimental outcome.
manufacturability_assessment: Matrixed experiments are implementable at bench scale with candidate formulation buffers and controlled freeze-thaw cycles; success would enable clear process gates without immediately requiring full GMP-scale runs. Yield and assay robustness must be evaluated before adoption as manufacturing criteria.
manufacturing_rationale: Defining permissible process-stage exposures (freeze-thaw, buffer composition) that preserve an intact-EV analytical signature would create actionable process acceptance gates, reduce CMC uncertainty, and enable reproducible lot definition and downstream potency assay development.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow before and after controlled process exposures: density-fractionation (iodixanol single-cushion or gradient) with particle counting per fraction, immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture detection of EV surface markers on intact material per fraction, detergent + protease/RNase protection assays on captured material, and total protein and protein:particle ratios per fraction. Include buffer-only interference controls and positive EV controls.
novelty_statement: Novel: This hypothesis specifically tests whether common downstream, bench-to-manufacturing-relevant exposures (quantified freeze-thaw cycles and contact with candidate nasal formulation buffers) — rather than source-cell attributes, fractionation method, or bulk particle counts — are sufficient to abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature. Prior hypotheses explored identity/fractionation, source-cell senescence, scalable isolation workflows, and in vivo bridging; none directly evaluated matrixed downstream processing exposures (freeze-thaw and formulation-buffer compatibility) as discrete, testable manufacturing-process gates. This experiment is a distinct discriminating test that isolates post-fractionation handling as a causal variable and includes assay-interference controls to separate true membrane disruption from analytic artifacts.
principal_risks: Assay interference by formulation buffers could mimic signature loss and lead to false-positive process failures.
Bench-scale findings may not translate to manufacture-scale; yield or stability tradeoffs may prevent practical acceptance gates.
If signature preservation cannot be achieved across required process steps, program may need to pivot to a secretome-centric product definition.
proposed_potency_relationship: If the intact-EV analytical signature is process-sensitive, only materials processed within defined acceptance windows that preserve the signature should be tested for potency linkage; otherwise potency attribution to intact EVs is uncertain.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, specify downstream-process acceptance conditions: permissible freeze-thaw exposure and formulation-buffer classes that preserve an orthogonal intact-EV-associated signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) as a manufacturing-process gate.
title: Process-stage sensitivity hypothesis: does freeze-thaw and formulation-buffer exposure during downstream processing disrupt the intact-EV-associated analytical signature?
